commentaryEvent.comment: It was a comfortable 62 point win for Hawthorn. The win was enough to secure a top-4 berth, but not enough for them to leapfrog Brisbane into third place. The Hawks dominated field position, winning the inside 50 count by 20 off the back of 30 forward half intercepts that resulted in 7.3.45.
The siren has sounded to end Q4.
Tylar Young has been a brick wall for the Eagles today with a match-high 10 spoils along with a team-high nine intercept possessions to compliment his 18 disposals.

Hawthorn have recorded the last seven inside 50s of the match before Jack Gunston finally gets the major the Hawks have been searching for. Gunston's last two seasons have been his two best seasons in front of goal with 76 and 59 goals respectively.

Will Day has four disposals, three score involvements and a goal in the final quarter as the Hawks press for the percentage boost needed to overtake Brisbane on the ladder. Day has been productive today with 21 disposals, nine contested possessions, six clearances, seven score involvements and two goals.

The stoppage game has been of less consequence than the forward half intercept game, but the Hawks have performed well in this area, leading the clearances by 11 and outscoring the Eagles 6.5.41 to 2.3.15 from this source.
In addition to Hawthorn outscoring West Coast 6.2.38 to 2.3.15 from forward half intercepts, the Hawks have also outscored the Eagles 2.2.14 to nil from forward 50 stoppages.
The siren has sounded to end Q3.
Eagles Interchange - Brandon Starcevich off due to the blood rule.

Milan Murdock has been West Coast's main avenue to goal tonight with three of the team's four goals. Murdock has 13 disposals at 77 per cent efficiency, four contested possessions and five score involvements, along with the three goals.
A hanger and resulting goal from Nick Watson has brought this game to life. Watson has been maximum impact today with 11 disposals, eight score involvements, 270 metres gained and three goals.
Hawthorn now have the first nine inside 50s of the third quarter and have an overall advantage of 21 in this measure. This includes an advantage of 19 to seven in repeat inside 50s.
Hawthorn have won the first three clearances and have also generated the first six inside 50s of the quarter, but have kicked just 1.1.7 from this advantage.
Hawthorn has now kicked 5.0.30 from 14 forward half intercepts compared to the 1.3.9 that West Coast has kicked from 12 forward half intercepts.

Connor Macdonald has been an important connector for the Hawks today. He has 14 disposals at an impressive 100 per cent efficiency given the conditions, along with six contested possessions and six score involvements.
The siren has sounded to end Q2.
Eagles Interchange - Tylar Young off due to the blood rule.
Hawthorn are starting to dominate territory, recording the last seven inside 50s of the match. For the term, the Hawks have enjoyed 64 per cent time in forward half.

The conditions have turned this contest into a forward half intercept game. The Hawks have 10 forward half intercepts, yielding them 3.0.18 while West Coast have eight forward half intercepts, resulting in just 1.2.8.

Hawthorn leads the tackle count by seven this quarter and by 13 for the match. Not surprisingly given the conditions, this is a high pressure game, with the Hawks leading the pressure rating 206 to 186.

Jack Gunston's four goals tonight put him on a total of 131 goals since the beginning of 2025, equal-most of any player along side Ben King. Gunston has played eight less games than King over the time period.

West Coast have been able to generate three scores from their first four inside 50s of the term and are winning the territory battle by virtue of their handball game. The Eagles have generated 334 metres gained by hand, compared to Hawthorn who have generated -15 metres by the same measure.
With the rain falling, the Hawks have yet to record an uncontested possession in the first five minutes of the term. Hawthorn had 20 more uncontested possessions than the Eagles in the opening term.

Hawthorn has made a strong start in its quest for third spot on the ladder, leading at quarter time by 29 points. The Hawks have been ruthless from stoppage, outscoring West Coast 4.1.25 to 1.1.7 from this source. When Hawthorn outscores its opposition from stoppage this season, they have won 10 out of 10 games.
The siren has sounded to end Q1.
West Coast have 22 kicks and 42 handballs for the match which is inviting the Hawthorn pressure. The Hawks have a pressure rating of 198, compared to West Coast's 181.
All five of Hawthorn's goals have come from set shots, with 4.0.24 coming from the four marks they have taken inside 50.
Hawthorn's ball use continues to be a feature of their play, kicking at an efficiency of 82 per cent by foot, which is in stark contrast to the 47 per cent efficiency of West Coast.
Hawthorn leads clearances five to two and have kicked an efficient 3.0.18 from these opportunities.
Eagles Interchange - Tylar Young off due to the blood rule.
Hawks Interchange - Dylan Moore off due to the blood rule.

Hawthorn hold an advantage in uncontested possession by 13, which includes an advantage of 17 to five in uncontested marks. Hawthorn's kicking efficiency is 86 per cent as a result, compared to just 50 per cent from the Eagles.

Hawthorn have the opening two centre bounce clearances of the game and have scored 2.0.12 from these chains. The Hawks rank sixth for points from centre bounce this season, averaging 14 points per game form this source.
The Eagles have lost the first possessions by seven and clearances by four per game this season, ranked 18th in each statistic.
The Hawks have taken a mark and immediately played on from 30 per cent of marks, the highest rate of any team.
